issues.legal_issue: For a post-dated cheque, the six-month period for presentation begins on the date written on the cheque, not the earlier date on which it was delivered.
material_facts: The drawer delivered the cheque before the date written on it; the cheque bore a later date.
The payee presented the cheque more than six months after delivery but within six months of the date written on it.
The cheque was returned unpaid with the endorsement that the account was closed.
The Magistrate took cognizance and issued process for the cheque-dishonour offence, and the drawer appealed against the refusal to quash the prosecution.
issues.conclusion: The post-dated cheque became a cheque on the date written on it, so the six-month presentation period ran from that date. Because it was presented within that period, the Court found no ground to quash the prosecution and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5 and 6 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, a post-dated instrument remains a bill of exchange until the date written on it, when it becomes a cheque payable on demand; Section 19 addresses instruments payable on demand. Under proviso (a) to Section 138, the presentation period is counted from the date the cheque is drawn. The Court applied Anil Kumar Sawhney v. Gulshan Rai, 1993 (4) SCC 424, which it followed, and relied on Jiwanlal Achariya v. Rameshwarlal Agarwalla, AIR 1967 SC 1118, in explaining the effect of conditional payment by post-dated cheque.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_process_for_cheque_dishonour and cheque_bears_later_date_than_delivery and presented_after_six_months_from_delivery and presented_within_six_months_of_face_date and cheque_returned_unpaid

predicates.appeal_challenges_process_for_cheque_dis: The proceeding is an appeal challenging cognizance or process for a cheque-dishonour offence.
predicates.cheque_bears_later_date_than_delivery: The drawer delivered a cheque bearing a date later than the date of delivery.
predicates.presented_after_six_months_from_delivery: The payee presented the cheque more than six months after receiving it.
predicates.presented_within_six_months_of_face_date: The payee presented the cheque within six months of the date written on it.
predicates.cheque_returned_unpaid: The bank returned the cheque unpaid.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges process for cheque dishonour and a post-dated cheque was presented after six months from delivery but within six months of its face date and was returned unpaid, the prosecution is not quashed.
